lecture_beats.subject: Discrete change, continuous phase-space flow, Hamilton equations, and Poisson brackets
Inner-product preservation, unitary evolution, the Hermitian generator, and the classical-limit question
Infinitesimal evolution and the abstract Schrodinger equation
Anisotropic polarization energies, relative phase, interference, and experimental questions
Expectation-value differentiation and the commutator evolution law
Commuting observables, conservation laws, and the classical analogy
Wave-function representation, momentum, and the free-particle Schrodinger equation
Momentum eigenstate, plane-wave time dependence, and momentum conservation

resolved_source_issues.issue: The lecture temporarily suppresses hbar while introducing the infinitesimal generator.
resolved_source_issues.resolution: The chapter retains hbar throughout so dimensions and the later Schrodinger equation remain explicit.

resolved_source_issues.issue: The analyzer derivation changes notation while expanding the cross terms.
resolved_source_issues.resolution: The overlap, conjugation, relative phase, and final probability are written in one consistent notation.

resolved_source_issues.issue: The spoken polarization description can suggest a linearly polarized state at all intermediate phases.
resolved_source_issues.resolution: The chapter distinguishes linear extrema, circular quarter-cycle states, and general elliptical states.

resolved_source_issues.issue: The commutator order and sign are corrected at the board.
resolved_source_issues.resolution: Both equivalent conventions are displayed and the audience correction is preserved.

resolved_source_issues.issue: The free-particle calculation repeatedly loses signs and hbar factors.
resolved_source_issues.resolution: The chapter derives p squared explicitly and restores the complete free Schrodinger equation.

resolved_source_issues.issue: The ideal momentum eigenstate is treated without a normalization qualification.
resolved_source_issues.resolution: The plane wave is identified as delta-normalized and localized states as superpositions.

resolved_source_issues.issue: The source video has limited image resolution.
resolved_source_issues.resolution: Frames preserve board evidence while all equations are independently typeset.

uncertain_sources.note: Handedness depends on propagation and viewing conventions; the chapter limits itself to the phase evolution needed here.
Self-adjointness depends on operator domains and boundary conditions, noted but not developed in this lecture.
The plane wave is an ideal generalized eigenstate rather than a normalizable one-particle packet.
